solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stays if worried about performer meeting requirements

indicators.note: about tells us the scrambled letters sit around the performer
worried suggests the letters of the words stays if being fretted into a new shape

parts.note: an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A nervous actor stays put, fretting about whether the show will go well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges the first two words; 'about' wraps that result round the performer, who sits just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adequate is one that meets the requirements set for it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Hang revolutionary American outlay!

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the American letters are read backwards

parts.note: to spend is to lay out money

explanation.surface: An American revolutionary's spending is enough to see him hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it from above.

clue.text: Temperature and skin infection? Rubbish!

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a fever and a rash as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash is a straight synonym for worthless rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: One goes off and hides large sum of money needed to support London?

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means standing underneath, so the money goes below the city

parts.note: the Smoke, or Big Smoke, is a slang name for London
a bomb is British slang for a lot of money

explanation.surface: A fortune is needed to keep London going.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SMOKE is an old British nickname for London; 'costs a bomb' means costs a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that explodes to release a cloud screens whatever is behind it.

clue.text: Jump on ice and cut line

parts.note: to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A skater jumps on the ice and slices a line through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A skating leap with one and a half turns, named after a Norwegian skater.

clue.text: Recognised artist holding up exchanges in commerce

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the held letters are read from the bottom
holding says the letters sit inside the words recognised artist

explanation.surface: A famous painter is busy with trading.
explanation.walkthrough: The run NISEDART across 'Recognised artist' is read upwards, as 'up' asks in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade something in is to hand it over as part payment in a deal.

clue.text: Sprays of flowers

definitions.meaning: nozzles that sprinkle water from a watering can

explanation.definitionFit: The perforated heads on watering cans share their name with the garden blooms.

clue.text: Quickly drink and go — there's a recession!

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it fast
a turn is a go

explanation.surface: Someone gulps a drink and leaves, fretting about the slump.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic slump is a decline in activity.

clue.text: Breaking the law may provide an abundance of material possessions

indicators.note: breaking suggests the letters of the law being smashed and put back together

explanation.surface: Crime may make you rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches are a great store of money and property.

clue.text: Continuing drama, like this artist pursuing a religious leader

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the artist comes after the rest

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
the Pope leads the Roman Catholic Church
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A drama compared to an artist chasing a pope through history.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial on television or radio that runs on and on is the classic continuing drama.

clue.text: Music written for twenty?

definitions.meaning: the written form of a piece of music for all its parts
an old word for a group of twenty

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard dictionary meanings: a composer's written music and a set of twenty.

clue.text: Traces of European Commission houses without us

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the word us from the word before it

parts.note: the word houses is taken as written
the word us is taken as written

explanation.surface: Brussels officials are housing people, but not us.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingering traces of something past are its reverberations or faint repetitions.

clue.text: Some compromise, as on a limit at a particular time of the year

definitions.text: at a particular time of the year

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deal that is struck only at a certain time of year, with a limit attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tied to the seasons happens only at a particular part of the year.

clue.text: A particularly intimidating woman doctor gets pain reduced

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the pain word is dropped

parts.note: agony is severe pain

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman doctor finds that her pain has eased.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, frightening woman is called a dragon in informal speech, after the fire-breathing monster.

clue.text: Lively article made it absurd

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: absurd suggests the words made it are twisted into nonsense

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece made something sound ridiculous but lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of energy and spirit, as in an animated discussion.

clue.text: Runs into president after broadcast to improve image

indicators.note: after puts the president with the inserted letter behind the broadcast word

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

indicators.note: into tells us the runs letter goes inside the president

parts.note: Bush was the name of two US presidents
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs into the president after a broadcast to polish their public profile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it only supplies the cricket letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: To retouch a photograph with a spray tool is to make a picture look better.

clue.text: Dance with the Queen at home — a pirouetting star!

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
in means at home

explanation.surface: Dancing with the Queen at home, a star spins round.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ballet dancer is the one who spins on her toes on stage.

clue.text: Glass preferably found outside church

indicators.note: found outside tells us the preference word goes round the church letters

parts.note: sooner means rather, by preference

explanation.surface: A drink would preferably be had outside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: A SCHOONER is a tall glass for sherry, or for beer in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A large drinking vessel, used for sherry in Britain and beer elsewhere.

clue.text: Story told to support cause of delay on the road

definitions.text: cause of delay on the road

indicators.note: told signals that the story word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tale is a story
to back something is to support it

explanation.surface: A tale told to justify why someone was held up in traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: A TAILBACK is the British word for a long queue of traffic stretching back from an obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A long queue of stationary vehicles is what holds drivers up on the road.

clue.text: Watch credit here, lacking protection

parts.note: on tick means on credit

indicators.note: lacking protection removes the outer letters that shield the word here

explanation.surface: Buy the watch on credit here, without insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for a timepiece (and also the heart).

clue.text: Songbird flying over lake — quail?

indicators.note: flying over pictures the bird spread above and around the lake letter, so it holds it

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird passes over a lake: could it be a quail?
explanation.walkthrough: 'quail' looks like another bird; here it is the verb meaning to shrink back in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to recoil or shrink in fear, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Practical lad follows script

indicators.note: follows places the lad after the script

parts.note: hand means handwriting, a script
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A youngster sticks to the script, very practical.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands-on describes direct, practical involvement rather than theory.

clue.text: Area for discussion of poor match played with no pressure

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of poor match being shuffled about like pieces in a game
with no tells us the pressure letter is taken out of the fodder

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A dull match was played with no pressure at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from POORMATCH, then 'played' rearranges the remaining OORMATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An online space where users exchange messages is a place set aside for conversation.

clue.text: Show runs rings around disheartened debutante

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: around puts the rings either side of the letters from the debutante

parts.note: O is ring-shaped, so two rings are OO

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, the inner letters, of debutante

explanation.surface: A show runs circles around a young society girl who has lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves DE from debutante; 'around' puts the two Os round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public show of cowboy skills.

clue.text: Put down all outsiders in dispute — more aggression

indicators.note: all outsiders in means take the first and last letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: In an argument, the side that pushes harder ends up humiliating the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade or belittle someone is to put them down.

clue.text: Tedium in French? Yes, in French, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the French words are spoken

parts.note: en is French for in and oui is French for yes, run together they are said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether boredom has a French word: yes, it does.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Visual problem caused by dropping line from fashion

indicators.note: dropping means the line letter falls out

parts.note: style is fashion

explanation.surface: A fashion faux pas becomes an eyesore.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an eye ailment.

clue.text: Finish after getting half of them correct

indicators.note: after getting places the finish word behind the half
half of picks out the second pair of letters of the word them

parts.note: an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a test after getting half the answers right.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text, removing errors, is to put it right.

clue.text: Run test in new substances that provide food

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of run test in being made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A trial is run to check fresh substances that give nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishing substances such as proteins and vitamins are what food supplies to the body.

clue.text: Pathetic story — it's a comparatively inferior thing

parts.note: poor means pathetic or inadequate
a relation is an account or narrative of events

explanation.surface: A sad tale is told about something that does not measure up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the weaker, lesser member of a group compared with its fellows.
